evidence.quote: A renal biopsy was also conducted (shown in Fig. 1, 2), which revealed findings consistent with PICGN.

Fig. 2.
Special staining for renal biopsy. HE staining: six glomeruli were observed, with no evidence of global or segmental glomerulosclerosis; PAS staining: focal tubular atrophy, interstitial edema, and scattered inflammatory cell infiltration were noted. Fibrosis was not prominent, and the arterial walls showed no significant thickening. There was no evidence of fibrinoid necrosis in the small arteries; PASM staining: granular degeneration of tubular epithelial cells was observed, along with red blood cell casts and occasional protein casts. Some tubules exhibited luminal dilation, epithelial cell detachment, loss of brush borders, and the formation of denuded basement membranes; Masson staining: six cellular-fibrous crescents were identified within the glomeruli, accompanied by fragmentation and collapse of capillary loops. Segmental fibrinoid necrosis was observed in one glomerular capillary loop.

evidence.quote: supplemented by immuno-electron microscopy of the renal biopsy (shown in Fig. 3)

Fig. 3.
Immune electron microscopy of kidney. Glomeruli: glomeruli exhibit crescent formation. Focal vacuolar degeneration of capillary endothelial cells is evident. Occasional lumina contain aggregated erythrocytes. Significant endothelial cell hyperplasia is not observed, and capillary loops are patent; basement membrane: segmental thickening is present, with thickness ranging from approximately 250–550 nm; visceral epithelial cells: podocytes appear swollen with vacuolar degeneration. Extensive foot process effacement is observed. Scant subepithelial electron-dense deposits are occasionally noted; mesangial area: mesangial hypercellularity and matrix expansion are present. No electron-dense deposits are detected in the mesangium; tubulointerstitium: tubular epithelial cells show vacuolar degeneration. Occasional tubular epithelial cells are denuded. Mild increases in cytoplasmic lysosomes are observed in some tubular epithelial cells. Interstitial edema is accompanied by mild inflammatory cell infiltration; interstitial vessels: occasional capillary lumina contain aggregated erythrocytes.
